text:
maria: Quick question — we need to finalize how Free/Pro/Enterprise map to enforcement and what shows up in Console. Two specific asks: (1) are bursts charged against org or key? (2) how should the UI display remaining burst capacity vs steady quota?

alex: my take: bursts should be accounted at the org level by default but fall back to per-key if org metadata is missing. avoids accidental sharing across teams in a single org with multiple keys.

jamal: +1 org-first. but curious about edge: if org hits steady limit and one key is in a canary test, do we allow a small tagged burst for that key? we had that request from infra earlier.

sophia: from PM side, customers expect plan entitlements to be obvious in the Billing/Limits page. showing two numbers (steady remaining, burst remaining) might be confusing — maybe show steady + a tooltip about "burst window" with examples. :thinking_face: 

maria: good point. product wants a single "Allowance" number where possible. but enforcement still needs both. so console could show allowance with a link to "details" that expands the burst/steady split.

alex: also: technical enforcement note — our rate engine currently evaluates per-key tokens then per-org aggregate in separate passes. implementing org-first burst would require atomically reserving burst capacity during evaluation to avoid double-counting. cheap sketch: evaluate key reservation, then decrement org bucket in same tx.

jamal: example policy we'd enforce: 
```json
{
  "plan":"pro",
  "steady_tokens_per_min":5000,
  "burst_tokens":20000,
  "burst_window_seconds":60,
  "billing_unit":"token"
}
```
this implies bursts are ephemeral and not billed as extra unless they exceed monthly committed units. we need to sync billing signals.

sophia: billing sync is huge. we should show "estimated burst usage" in console to prevent surprises. maybe a warning when someone is within 80% but has a 10x burst pattern.

infra-bot: deploy-check: rate-engine/v2 has tests for per-key and org-aggregate; 6 failing currently (race on concurrent reservations). See CI: https://ci.internal/12345

maria: on the UI copy — proposed lines: 
- "Allowance: 5,000 tokens/min (burst: 20,000 tokens over 60s)"
- link: "How bursts work" -> expand with short animated example

alex: UX nit: include a small histogram showing recent burst usage (30m). that'll make it obvious if a customer is spiky.

jamal: ops question: when we fallback from org->key enforcement, do we inherit the org's burst policy or keep key-level limits? i prefer inherit org policy so keys can't bypass.

sophia: agree on inherit. but we must show that in the Console under each API key row: "Entitlement: Inherits org (Pro)" or "Custom limits".

maria: decision proposal: 
1) Enforcement: org-first, per-key fallback. org policy is authoritative and inherited by keys unless key has explicit custom limits.
2) Billing: bursts are metered but only billed when monthly committed units are exceeded; console shows estimated burst consumption.
3) Console UX: primary metric = "Allowance" (steady), secondary = collapsible "Burst details" + 30m spark histogram and warning thresholds.
4) Implementation: rate-engine must perform atomic two-phase reserve (key -> org) to avoid double reservations; add tests for concurrency.

alex: will spike implementation this afternoon. I'll add ticket with the tx sketch and link tests.

sophia: I'll update the mock in Figma and send to maria for copy.

maria: thanks — can everyone add objections by EOD? if none, i'll put this into the roadmap. :thumbsup:

jamal: noted — I'll add a canary run plan for a single key with explicit "canary-burst" flag to test inherit vs override.

sophia: done — Figma link: https://figma.internal/s/fw-allowance-v2

maria: great, closing unless objections. thanks all.
